title: Orionid Meteor Shower Peaks This Week in WV, KY & OH

content:
(WOWK) — The weather is set to cooperate with sky watchers trying to see the Orionid meteor shower as it peaks on the night of October 21-22.

A week of high pressure and dry air means a lot of clear skies and chances to witness a meteor for those with patience and luck. The StormTracker 13 Predictor model shows barely any clouds around as the meteor shower peaks the night of October 21-22 which is Wednesday night crossing into Thursday morning. Temperatures for sky watchers during the overnight hours will generally be in the 40s for most of the nights during the week.

According to Tony Rice with NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the best views are after the Moon sets around 2:43 AM on Thursday morning.

Those looking for a fireworks-style show will likely be let down as this meteor shower typically produces around 10 to 20 meteors each hour in a dark sky for viewing at the peak. Those statistics reflect the perfect conditions for someone in totally dark conditions. With the moonlight at about 75-80 percent, it would be much more realistic to see about 3 meteors of significant brightness per hour if you were in Charleston according to info supplied by Rice to StormTracker 13. While that may sound a little disappointing, there have also been years where 50-75 meteors have been produced and witnessed. It’s all a matter of how much space dust the comet Halley wants to leave behind it for us to witness.

The name “Orionid” comes from the fact that the showers appear to emanate from the constellation Orion in the southeastern skies. The best advice to see the meteor shower is to look generally southeast and up and stay away from as many city lights as you can.

If you miss the peak, the meteor shower goes on until the end of the first week of November or so for stargazers to try to give seeing one another chance.
